questions.question: What are some human rights concerns in India?
questions.solution_html:
• Human rights issues in India include rising violence against religious minorities and Dalits
  • restrictions on freedom of expression and media, and use of repressive laws against activists.
  • Significant concerns involve police impunity, caste-based violence, forced evictions, and
  • ethnic clashes, particularly in regions like Manipur and Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.final_answer: ethnic clashes, particularly in regions like Manipur and Jammu and Kashmir
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is the difference between gender identity and gender expression?
questions.solution_html:
• Gender identity is a person's deep internal sense of being a man, woman, neither, or both
  • while gender expression is how they outwardly present their gender to the world through
  • clothing, behaviour, and appearance. Identity is internal and personal; expression is external
  • and communicative.
questions.final_answer: and communicative
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Give an example of human rights violation.
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Write any two roles of NHRC.
questions.solution_html:
• Key roles of the NHRC include
  •  Investigative & Preventive Role: It has the power to inquire into violations of human
  • rights (such as custodial deaths or police excesses). It can also visit jails and detention
  • centres to monitor the living conditions of inmates.
  •  Advisory & Evaluative Role: It reviews the effectiveness of existing laws and
  • constitutional protections for human rights and advises the government on
  • implementing international human rights treaties.
questions.final_answer: implementing international human rights treaties
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What do gender roles determine?
questions.solution_html:
• The gender roles include
  •  Division of Labour: Traditionally, this sets roles like breadwinner for men and
  • nurturer/homemaker for women.
  •  Occupational Choices: Gender Roles influence which professions are deemed
  • appropriate, creating occupational segregation, such as women in caregiving roles and

questions.question: Write the importance of fundamental duties in promoting human rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Fundamental duties promote human rights include
  •  Balancing Rights and Obligations: Duties act as a moral counterpart to Fundamental
  • Rights, ensuring that rights are not exercised in a vacuum but with responsibility
  • toward the community.
  •  Preventing Abuse of Rights: They act as a warning against actions that violate the
  • rights of others, such as damaging public property or promoting communal
  • disharmony.
questions.final_answer: disharmony

questions.question: What is the concept of indivisibility of human rights?
questions.solution_html:
• The indivisibility of human rights is the principle that all rights—civil, political, economic
  • social, and cultural—are inseparable, equal in importance, and inherent to human dignity. No
  • right is superior to another, and the enjoyment of one often depends on the realization of
  • others.

questions.question: Describe the different types of genders.
questions.solution_html:
• The different gender identities are
  •  Cisgender: People whose gender identity matches the sex they were assigned at birth.
  •  Transgender: An umbrella term for people whose gender identity differs from the sex
  • they were assigned at birth (e.g., trans man, trans woman).
  •  Non-binary: A spectrum of gender identities that are not exclusively masculine or
  • feminine, falling outside the traditional male-female binary.
  •  Agender: People who do not identify with any gender, or who feel they have no
  • gender.
  •  Genderfluid: Someone whose gender identity is not fixed and shifts or fluctuates over
  • time.
  •  Genderqueer: A term for people who do not subscribe to conventional gender
  • distinctions and may blend or move between genders.
questions.final_answer: distinctions and may blend or move between genders
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Comment in detail on biological sex and gender.
questions.solution_html:
• Comment in detail on biological sex and gender.
  • Biological Sex
  •  Definition: Based on physiological features—chromosomes and hormones
  •  Assignment: Assigned at birth as male or female based on physical appearance.
  • Gender
  •  Definition: The socially constructed roles, behaviours, expressions, and identities that
  • society considers appropriate for men, women, and gender-diverse people.
  •  Components
  • o Gender Identity: An internal, deeply felt sense of self (e.g., man, woman
  • nonbinary).
  • o Gender Expression: How a person presents their gender outwardly, such as
  • through clothing or behaviour.
  • o Gender Roles: Social expectations of how to act or behave based on assigned
  • sex.
questions.final_answer: sex
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Analyse the role of HR in preventing and addressing work place harassment.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the role of HR in preventing and addressing work place harassment.
  • HR's Role in Prevention of work place harassment
  •  Policy Development & Communication: HR must create clear, comprehensive anti
  • harassment policies that define prohibited conduct, reporting procedures, and
  • consequences.
  •  Training & Education: Regular, mandatory workshops for all staff and specialized
  • training for leadership/investigation committees (such as IC in India) ensure
  • awareness.
  •  Cultural Transformation: Actively promoting a respectful, safe, and inclusive
  • environment through communication channels like posters, emails, and meetings.
questions.final_answer: environment through communication channels like posters, emails, and meetings
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain in detail gender expression.
questions.solution_html:
• Gender expression is the external manifestation of a person’s gender, displayed through
  • clothing, hairstyle, makeup, mannerisms, speech patterns, and behaviours. It is how
  • individuals present their gender to the world, which may or may not align with their internal
  • gender identity or societal expectations of masculinity or feminine
  • Key aspects of Gender Expression
  •  External Presentation: Unlike internal gender identity, expression is how one is
  • perceived by others.
  •  Social & Cultural Norms: Expression is interpreted based on societal stereotypes
  • such as masculine, feminine, or androgynous.
  •  Independence from Identity/Sex: A person’s expression does not have to match their
  • biological sex or their internal sense of gender.
questions.final_answer: biological sex or their internal sense of gender
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Discuss the causes of gender discrimination in society
questions.solution_html:
• Primary Causes of Gender Discrimination
  •  Patriarchal Society and Gender Roles: A dominant structure where men hold power
  • influencing family and societal decisions. Society often expects women to adhere
  • strictly to caregiving roles, limiting their potential.
  •  Social Customs and Beliefs: Deep-seated preferences for male children and the
  • devaluation of daughters lead to discrimination, including dowry systems, sex
  • selective abortions, and neglect of the girl child.
  •  Economic Disparity and Dependency: Women often face lower wages, fewer career
  • opportunities, and a lack of ownership or inheritance rights, forcing economic
  • dependency on male counterparts.
  •  Lack of Education and Literacy: Educational imbalances, particularly in developing
  • areas, restrict girls' opportunities, limiting their awareness of rights and ability to
  • challenge norms.
questions.final_answer: challenge norms
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the different concepts of human rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Characteristics of Human Rights
  •  Universal: Applicable to everyone across the globe, as stated in the Universal
  • Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR).
  •  Inalienable: They cannot be taken away or surrendered, except in specific, lawful
  • situations.
  •  Indivisible and Interdependent: All rights (civil, political, social) are equally
  • important and connected; one cannot fully enjoy one set of rights without the others.
questions.final_answer: important and connected; one cannot fully enjoy one set of rights without the others
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the powers and functions of National Human Rights Commission.
questions.solution_html:
• Functions of the NHRC
  •  Inquiry: Investigates human rights violations or negligence by public servants through
  • petitions.
  •  Court Intervention: Intervenes in court proceedings involving human rights issues
  • with court permission.
  •  Jail Inspections: Visits jails and detention centres to study living conditions and
  • recommend improvements.
  •  Legal Review: Reviews constitutional and legal safeguards for human rights
  • protection and recommends effective implementation measures.
  • Powers of the NHRC
  •  Civil Court Powers: While investigating, the commission acts as a civil court.
  •  Investigation Team: It has its own investigative staff to examine complaints.
  •  Recommendations: Can recommend compensation to victims or prosecution of the
  • guilty to governments.
  •  Immediate Action: Can recommend interim relief to victims.
questions.final_answer:  Immediate Action: Can recommend interim relief to victims
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

  • HR's Role in Prevention of work place harassment
  •  Policy Development & Communication: HR must create clear, comprehensive anti
  • harassment policies that define prohibited conduct, reporting procedures, and
  • consequences.
  •  Training & Education: Regular, mandatory workshops for all staff and specialized

  • awareness.

questions.question: Explain in detail gender expression.
questions.solution_html:
• Gender expression is the external manifestation of a person’s gender, displayed through
  • clothing, hairstyle, makeup, mannerisms, speech patterns, and behaviours. It is how
  • individuals present their gender to the world, which may or may not align with their internal
  • gender identity or societal expectations of masculinity or feminine
  • Key aspects of Gender Expression
  •  External Presentation: Unlike internal gender identity, expression is how one is
  • perceived by others.
  •  Social & Cultural Norms: Expression is interpreted based on societal stereotypes
  • such as masculine, feminine, or androgynous.
  •  Independence from Identity/Sex: A person’s expression does not have to match their
  • biological sex or their internal sense of gender.
questions.final_answer: biological sex or their internal sense of gender

questions.question: Discuss the causes of gender discrimination in society
questions.solution_html:
• Primary Causes of Gender Discrimination
  •  Patriarchal Society and Gender Roles: A dominant structure where men hold power
  • influencing family and societal decisions. Society often expects women to adhere
  • strictly to caregiving roles, limiting their potential.
  •  Social Customs and Beliefs: Deep-seated preferences for male children and the
  • devaluation of daughters lead to discrimination, including dowry systems, sex
  • selective abortions, and neglect of the girl child.
  •  Economic Disparity and Dependency: Women often face lower wages, fewer career
  • opportunities, and a lack of ownership or inheritance rights, forcing economic
  • dependency on male counterparts.
  •  Lack of Education and Literacy: Educational imbalances, particularly in developing
  • areas, restrict girls' opportunities, limiting their awareness of rights and ability to
  • challenge norms.
questions.final_answer: challenge norms

questions.question: Explain the different concepts of human rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Characteristics of Human Rights
  •  Universal: Applicable to everyone across the globe, as stated in the Universal
  • Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR).
  •  Inalienable: They cannot be taken away or surrendered, except in specific, lawful
  • situations.
  •  Indivisible and Interdependent: All rights (civil, political, social) are equally
  • important and connected; one cannot fully enjoy one set of rights without the others.
questions.final_answer: important and connected; one cannot fully enjoy one set of rights without the others
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the powers and functions of National Human Rights Commission.
questions.solution_html:
• Functions of the NHRC
  •  Inquiry: Investigates human rights violations or negligence by public servants through
  • petitions.
  •  Court Intervention: Intervenes in court proceedings involving human rights issues
  • with court permission.
  •  Jail Inspections: Visits jails and detention centres to study living conditions and
  • recommend improvements.
  •  Legal Review: Reviews constitutional and legal safeguards for human rights
  • protection and recommends effective implementation measures.
  • Powers of the NHRC
  •  Civil Court Powers: While investigating, the commission acts as a civil court.
  •  Investigation Team: It has its own investigative staff to examine complaints.
  •  Recommendations: Can recommend compensation to victims or prosecution of the
  • guilty to governments.
  •  Immediate Action: Can recommend interim relief to victims.
questions.final_answer:  Immediate Action: Can recommend interim relief to victims
